hints: Picture n amino acids in a row like beads on a string. How many joins do you need to link them all into one chain?
Remember what is lost when a peptide bond forms (water from COOH and NH2) and what is kept untouched on every amino acid.
walkthrough:
**Recall how a peptide bond forms**

Think of condensation. The COOH group of one amino acid joins to the NH2 group of the next, releasing water.

So a peptide bond is the link *between* two amino acids.

**Count the peptide bonds**

If you have 2 amino acids, you need 1 bond. If you have 3, you need 2 bonds. The pattern is always one less than the number of units.

$$ \text{peptide bonds} = n - 1 $$

**Count the R groups**

Every single amino acid has its own central carbon with its own R group (side chain). This R group is not used up in forming the peptide bond.

So n amino acids still bring n R groups into the polypeptide. That gives $n-1$ bonds and $n$ R groups.

options.A: Peptide bonds are correct as n-1, but R groups are wrong. No R group is lost when peptide bonds form, so there are still n of them.
options.B: Exactly right. n amino acids are joined by n-1 peptide bonds, and each amino acid keeps its own R group, so n R groups.
options.C: Both parts are wrongly counted. You do not need n bonds to join n units, and you do not lose an R group.
options.D: R groups are correct as n, but peptide bonds are wrong. n amino acids need only n-1 links to make one continuous chain.
